readme: Reviewed measure-kind mismatches for audit-unit-basis-outlier.ps1. A cell lands here when its size names a different KIND of quantity than its shelf-mates (a volume among weights, or the reverse) but the NUMBER is still right, so the published per-unit is correct. That is the ordinary case for products whose density is near water, and for pack sizes a store states in one unit and the capture converts to the other. Keyed on commodity + store + the exact SIZE STRING that was reviewed: change the size and the review is void and the guard speaks up again, which is what stops a blanket per-store silence. NEVER add an entry to make the guard green - the entry has to say why the NUMBER is right, not why the flag is annoying. A cell whose number is wrong is fixed with a commodity exclude or add-known-wrong.ps1, not here (butter's pancake syrup and baby-formula's ready-to-feed liquid were both fixed that way on 2026-08-08, not allowlisted).

allow.reason: The can is 18.8 oz by WEIGHT - the product name says '18.8 OZ' - and the size field labelled the same number as fl oz. Same number either way, so the per-oz figure is correct.
A 32 fl oz water-based spray on a commodity priced per oz. Density is within a few percent of water, so fl oz and oz are interchangeable here at the precision the board publishes.
The product name states '12 oz' and the size field states '12 fl oz'. Same number, opposite label, so the per-unit is unaffected.
The product name states '200.2 Fl Oz' and the size field states '200.303 oz'. The row is priced per fl oz; the two numbers agree to within 0.05%, so the label is the only thing that differs.
Mt. Olive 1 gal. One gallon is 128 fl oz and pickle brine is near water, so 126.8 oz is a faithful weight conversion of the stated gallon rather than a basis error.
Member's Mark 1 gal. Ranch dressing runs about 1.06 g/ml, so 128 fl oz is roughly 135.7 oz by weight - 135.25 is a faithful conversion of the stated gallon, not a mismeasure.
